name: Pro Rata, Follow-On Capacity, and Pay-to-Play

positioning.oneLineSummary: Separates the legal right to participate, the fund's capacity and decision to participate, and the consequences of declining.
positioning.productLabel: Follow-On Rights Lens — based on Feld and Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials
notAClaimOf: a fund having enough reserves to exercise a right
pay-to-play creating an unconditional lifetime funding commitment

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public pro-rata and pay-to-play materials

neutralParaphrase: A pro-rata right creates conditional access to future financings; a fund still needs capacity, eligibility, allocation, approval, and a fresh underwriting decision. Pay-to-play may penalize nonparticipation in a qualifying round. Model rights, capacity, choice, and consequence separately for every investor and scenario.

locator.value: Pro-rata as the right to continue investing to maintain ownership
Qualified financing, required participation, affiliate aggregation, and preferred-to-common consequence
Chapter 5 pay-to-play; Chapter 7 first-refusal and other rights; Chapter 12 reserves and fund mechanics

requiredConditions: Eligibility, major-investor threshold, pro-rata formula, transfer, notice, allocation, and exclusions are exact.
Pay-to-play qualified-financing trigger, required amount, consequence, affiliates, waiver, and exceptions are exact.
Fund reserves, concentration, remaining life, follow-on policy, and approval are separately available.

requiredEvidence.description: Investor eligibility, pro-rata calculation, major-investor threshold, notice, transfer, allocation, and round exclusions.
Qualified-financing definition, participation requirement, affiliate aggregation, conversion or rights-loss consequence, waiver, and exceptions.
Available reserves, concentration, fund life, follow-on allocation policy, approvals, and opportunity cost.
Current company, market, terms, dilution, valuation, and expected-return analysis.

decisionQuestions: Does this investor legally have a pro-rata or other participation right?
How much may or must it invest, and by when?
Will allocation or new-lead conditions limit exercise?
Does the fund have approved capacity and concentration room?
What happens if the investor declines under pay-to-play?
Does the current underwrite justify exercising the right?
What other portfolio use competes for the reserve?
positiveSignals: Rights, eligibility, and deadlines are exact.
Fund capacity and approval are verified.
The company passes a fresh underwriting process.
Ownership retention and security payoff are modeled.
Decline and pay-to-play consequences are explicit.
redFlags: Pro-rata is treated as guaranteed allocation.
The fund is assumed to have reserves.
A contractual right substitutes for a fresh underwrite.
Super-pro-rata or transfer rights crowd out future financing without analysis.
disconfirmingEvidence: Major-investor status or ownership threshold has lapsed.
The round is excluded or notice was missed.
Fund reserve, concentration, or life prevents participation.
New terms or company evidence fail the current underwrite.
A waiver or alternative financing changes pay-to-play consequences.
contraindications: Do not equate right, capacity, and decision.
Do not exercise based on sunk cost or prior thesis alone.
Do not let the LLM calculate allocation or fund capacity.

instructions: Validate contractual eligibility, amount, allocation, and deadline.
Validate fund reserves, concentration, life, and approval.
Run a fresh underwriting and compare opportunity cost.
Send rights, economics, and policy outputs to deterministic Decision Policy.

sourceReliability.low: Rights or reserves rely on memory or verbal claims.
sourceReliability.medium: Contracts and fund data exist but allocation or pay-to-play details are incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Executed rights, current round, reserves, policy, and approvals reconcile.

evidenceStrength.low: Only a presumed right is known.
evidenceStrength.medium: Right and capacity are known but underwrite or allocation is uncertain.
evidenceStrength.high: Right, capacity, allocation, consequence, and underwrite are independently supported.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Right and round are covered but fund policy or consequence is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Eligibility, amount, allocation, deadline, consequence, fund capacity, underwrite, and opportunity cost are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: No follow-on right or financing exists.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: A right exists with custom exclusions or allocation.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The right and financing state are explicit.

judgmentConfidence.medium: A feasible participation range can be shown.
judgmentConfidence.high: All inputs are ready for Fund Policy decision.

promotionRequirements: Backtest follow-on decision and opportunity-cost workflow.
empiricalQualifications: Actual allocation may differ from contractual maximum.
Fund capacity and priorities change over time.
Follow-on returns are subject to selection, valuation, and survivorship effects.

rights.notes: Public author doctrine is neutrally paraphrased; contractual and fund-policy facts remain deal-specific.

openIssues: Map super-pro-rata and SAFE pro-rata variants.
